sources: Iran Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, televised speech, via Tasnim / Al Mayadeen / Arab News / Al Arabiya
fault_line: Trigger or table: Ghalibaf says Iran is ready for battle and has answered rationally -- is the ball really in Washington's court, or is this Tehran daring Trump to strike after the midterms?

sections.what_happened: Ghalibaf said Iran has given Washington a 'powerful and rational' / 'strong and rational' response, is at its highest level of defensive readiness, stands ready for battle 'with its finger on the trigger', and that 'the ball is now in America's court to prevent war'. He warned a further US 'strategic mistake' would open a new battlefield from which the US would struggle to find a way out. Separately, Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned a new war could endanger regional undersea cables, data centres and AI facilities it estimated at $2 trillion (via Kurdistan24 text). UNVERIFIED ADD-ON, NOT COUNTED: Kurdistan24 (NO declared tier in the registry) adds that Gulf officials say the US warned them larger strikes could come as early as November 4 -- single untiered source, no second family, do not publish as a date. Ghalibaf's Monday position (progress only once Iran's seven conditions are agreed) is restated context, not new.
sections.what_verified: Speech wording carried by two declared-tier families (Arab News T3, Al Arabiya T3, both Saudi/regional). Tasnim (originating agency per ednews) has NO declared tier and is NOT counted; Kurdistan24 likewise NOT counted, so its November 4 claim adds no family.
sections.what_disputed: The speech's own dual track (ready for battle + rational response) mirrors the day's pattern: US officials simultaneously describe the Qeshm strikes as limited/defensive (1200-04) while Trump/Vance tout a deal 'could happen' (0100-01, 0200-02). No agreement, text or date has been announced; Reuters via Al Mayadeen the same morning says mediators are narrowing gaps but Tehran and Washington 'remain far from reaching an agreement'.
sections.why_matters: The morning after the Qeshm strike, Tehran's chief negotiator speaks: finger on the trigger, rational answer given, ball in America's court. The speech is verified; the November 4 warning attached to it is not -- keep them separate on screen.
